plan.reason: The prior needs_more_evidence review identified that the bundled Respawn Script (index 18) polls Humanoid.Health and automatically clones/reparents the dummy while destroying the original whenever Health drops below 1, which directly contradicts req-dummy-target's mandatory acceptance criteria that the target 'never takes damage, ragdolls, resets, or respawns' and remains visually unchanged through repeated hits. This repair removes that script subtree entirely rather than stubbing it, since its only function is the forbidden reset/reclone behavior and it has no other useful logic worth preserving. All reusable mannequin geometry (Parts, Head, Torso, meshes, Humanoid) and the Torso decal are retained unmodified. No other component in this capture supplies hit-counting logic, so req-hit-counter remains dependent on the separately owned PunchServer integration task as already noted; that dependency is not resolved here and is restated in remainingIntegration.

removeSubtrees.reason: This Script clones script.Parent at load, then in an infinite polling loop checks Humanoid.Health<1 and, when true, waits 1s, reparents a cloned copy into script.Parent.Parent via makeJoints(), and removes the original — an automatic respawn/reset of the dummy. This is the exact behavior req-dummy-target forbids ('never...respawns', 'does not fall over or respawn'). The script contains no other logic (no hit detection, no counter, no decoration), so removing it loses no useful behavior while eliminating the disqualifying defect.

preservedBehavior: All static geometry Parts (indices 3,5,7,9,10,11,12) and their SpecialMesh children (4,6,8) are retained unmodified, preserving the mannequin's collidable shape for future touch/proximity hit-detection.

Head (13) and Torso (15) Parts with their SpecialMesh (14) and Decal (16, texture rbxassetid://406436910) are retained unmodified for visual appearance; the decal remains an unverified media reference pending later load/rights audit, not altered by this edit.

Humanoid (17) is retained so the model keeps a standard humanoid presence (e.g., for any future health-related UI or collision assumptions), but with the auto-respawn Script removed it no longer reacts to Health changes by cloning/destroying itself.
Overall Model/Training Dummy hierarchy (1, 2) and joint structure between parts is unchanged, so the dummy can still be anchored/placed at the approved position [0,3,12] as a single rigid assembly.
remainingIntegration: req-hit-counter and req-hit-detection still require the separately owned PunchServer component to add its own runtime touch/proximity or raycast listeners against this dummy's Parts (e.g., Torso/Head); no working hit-detection connection is established by this capture or this edit.

The Torso Decal texture (rbxassetid://406436910) remains an unverified media reference — its load, rights, and visual appearance have not been checked and must be confirmed during native/media verification before final acceptance.

With Humanoid (17) retained but no damage source in this game design (no player-damage mechanic per requirements), Health will not decrease during normal play; however, if any future script intentionally or accidentally sets Humanoid.Health<1, no respawn/reset code remains to react to it — this should be confirmed by native inspection rather than assumed.

Placement/anchoring at approximately [0,3,12] and CanCollide=true across all Parts must be confirmed in Studio; this capture provides geometry but placement is an integration task owned by targetDummySetup, not completed by this edit.
nativeTestPlan: In Studio, open the edited Training Dummy model and confirm index 18 (Script named 'Respawn') is no longer present under the model, with no other script remaining in its place.

Manually set the Humanoid's Health property to 0 in the Properties panel while the game is running in Studio and observe for at least 5 seconds that the dummy does NOT clone itself, does NOT reparent a duplicate, and the original instance is NOT removed — confirming the reset behavior is eliminated.
Verify all Parts (3,5,7,9,10,11,12,13,15) still have CanCollide=true and remain in their original relative positions/joints after the edit, with no visual change to the mannequin's appearance.

Confirm the Torso Decal (index 16, rbxassetid://406436910) still renders on the Torso part in Studio's 3D viewport as a basic visibility check; note that rights/appearance verification remains a separate deferred media check.

After PunchServer's touch/proximity listeners are implemented in the dependent component, native-test that repeated simulated hits against this dummy's Parts do not trigger any respawn/clone behavior and that the dummy remains a single persistent instance across many hits.
